notes:
Net map: 0 = bottom rail / reference, set by GND 7 whose stem is the continuation of Resistor 6's bottom lead down x~206 to the bars at y=291,295; the same node carries the right lead of Resistor 3 (3k) and the left lead of Inductor 5. n1 = V-DC 0 plus (top) lead up to y~198 and right to the left end of Resistor 4 (10 ohm). n2 = top node: right end of Resistor 4 -> T at (208,204) down to the top of Resistor 6 (7 ohm) -> right to the left lead of I-DC 1 (9 mA). n3 = right lead of I-DC 1 -> right at y~205 -> down at x~312 to the top plate of Capacitor 2 (6 uF). n4 = bottom plate of Capacitor 2 -> down at x~317 to y~280 -> left to the right end of Inductor 5 (12 H). n5 = V-DC 0 minus (bottom) lead down to y~275 and right to the left end of Resistor 3.
Judgment calls: (a) The bottom-left wire is broken in the scan: Resistor 3's right stub stops at x=176,y=278 and the next ink on that line is at x=202-207,y=277-279 where it meets the ground stem (pixel-level check at 14x; the source jpg is 4-level quantised so light pencil is dropped entirely - the same wire is dashed again between x=208-223 on its way to the inductor). I read the whole y~278 horizontal as ONE continuous wire, so Resistor 3's right end is on net 0. Rationale: leaving it open would leave the 2 V source with no return path, and would leave Resistor 6 + GND as a two-terminal dead-end branch carrying no current, i.e. a meaningless problem; the two stubs are collinear and point at each other.
(b) The horizontal at y~278 crosses the vertical GND stem at (206,278) with no dot and no hop - the strokes simply merge. I treated it as a JUNCTION (one node) rather than a crossover, again from circuit sense: as a crossover the 7 ohm shunt would be a dead end and the ground reference would touch only one component. This is the single most consequential call in this file and is the thing a human should re-check.
(c) Terminal order: V-DC 0 top(+) first then bottom(-); Capacitor 2 and Resistor 6 top then bottom; Resistors 3/4 and Inductor 5 left then right; the I-DC arrow points right but 2-terminal order is not metric-relevant.
(d) No off-frame components: all 8 bbox centres are inside the frame and no circuit wire leaves the crop (the long rectangle around the whole drawing is the notebook page border, not a wire).
